title: CRLR/253/2007 of HEM CHANDRA JOSHI Vs STATE

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 253 of 2007
Hem Chandra Joshi ............. Revisionist
 versus
State of Uttaranchal ............. Respondent
Mr. B.S. Adhikari, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. M.A. Khan, AGA and Ms. Meena Bohara, Brief Holder for the
respondent State.
Hon'ble U.C. Dhyani, J. (oral)

PW1 Sanjeev Bhatt wrote a complaint on
09.04.2005, at 11:30 A.M., to Inspector-In-Charge,
Kotwali Champawat against driver Hem Chandra Joshi,
which was registered as case crime no. 42 of 2005
under Sections 279, 337, 338, 304-A of IPC. After the
investigation, a charge-sheet was submitted against the
accused for the selfsame offences. When the
allegations were put to the accused, he denied those
allegations and said that his vehicle MAX CAB fell in
the gorge in order to save a Canter (mini truck).
2) Prosecution examined PW1 Sanjeev Bhatt,
informant/injured; PW2 Vivek Gaur, injured; PW3
Vipin Gupta, injured; PW4 Prem Karki, Photographer;
PW5 Chandra Sehkar Pandey, injured; PW6 S.I.
Shesram, formal witness; PW7 Dr. R.K. Joshi, Medical
Officer; PW8 S.I. Ram Swaroop Singh, formal witness;
PW9 Dr. V.K. Ozha, Medical Officer; PW10 Dr. R.D.
Bhatt, Medical Officer; PW11 S.I. Neeraj Kumar,

2
Investigating Officer; PW12 Dr. Pramod Dubey,
Medical Officer and PW13 H.C.M.T. Jaman Singh as
prosecution witnesses. Incriminating evidence was put
to the accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C., in reply to
which he said that he was falsely implicated in the
criminal case. No evidence was adduced in defence.
3) After considering the evidence on record,
learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Champawat found
the accused guilty and convicted him for the offences
punishable under Sections 279, 337, 338, 304-A of IPC
and was sentenced appropriately, vide judgment and
order dated 14.07.2006. Aggrieved against the said
order, criminal appeal was preferred before learned
Sessions Judge, Champawat, who dismissed the
criminal appeal, vide impugned judgment and order
dated 04.12.2007. Aggrieved against the impugned
judgment and order, present criminal revision was
preferred by the convict.
4) The incident took place on 09.04.2005, at
07:30 A.M., and the FIR was lodged on the selfsame
day at 11:30 A.M. The distance between the place of
incident and the police station concerned was 14
kilometers and, hence, there appears to be no delay in
lodging the FIR.
5) On 09.04.2005, at 05:30 A.M., PW1
alongwith other passengers boarded on ill-fated vehicle

3
bearing registration no. UA-03 / 3080 MAX CAB,
which was being driven by accused Hem Chandra
Joshi. The jeep was coming from Tanakpur to
Pithoragarh. At around 07:30 A.M., the jeep fell in a
gorge near village Dhon. The accused was driving the
vehicle rashly and negligently. Kedar Singh, resident
of village Jamredi, died. Other passengers sustained
injuries. Injured passengers were taken to Government
Hospital, Champawat for treatment. When informant
Sanjeev Bhatt entered into the witness box as PW1, he
proved his complaint (Ext. Ka-1), and also proved the
contents of the same. PW1 was also one of the injured
passengers. In the cross-examination, PW1 said that he
himself did not go to the police station carrying Ext.
Ka-1. He did not know the name of the driver prior to
the accident. PW1 came to know of the name of the
driver when he boarded the jeep. PW1 wrote the
complaint in the hospital. The accident took place all
of a sudden. In reply to the question of trial court, PW1
said that no vehicle was coming from the front of MAX
CAB. PW1 also said that the road was wide enough to
accommodate two vehicles at a time. It was not
narrow. PW1 denied the suggestion that the accident
took place in order to save a vehicle coming from the
front. Nothing came in the cross-examination of PW1
to suspect his testimony. He was an eyewitness as well
as an injured, whose presence inside the vehicle cannot
be doubted.

4
6) PW2 supported PW1 and reiterated that the
driver of MAX CAB drove the vehicle rashly and
negligently, as a consequence of which, the jeep fell
into a gorge, in which Kedar Singh died immediately
and others sustained injuries, who were taken to
Government Hospital. PW2 too was cross-examined.
PW2 also said that the accident took place all of a
sudden. The road was wide enough to accommodate
two vehicles. In this way, nothing came in the cross-examination of PW2 to suspect his testimony.
7) PW3 supported PW1 and PW2. PW3 was
also a natural witness, who boarded on the MAX CAB.
PW3's testimony was also acceptable. PW4 took the
photographs at the place of accident. PW5 also boarded
on the MAX CAB. PW5 also sustained injuries in the
accident. He also reiterated that the driver was driving
the vehicle rashly and negligently. PW5 said that the
road was wide. It was not narrow. In this way, PW5
also supported PW1, PW2 and PW3. PW6 was a
formal witness, who proved chik FIR (Ext. Ka-2) and
entry of the same in the G.D. (Ext. Ka-3).
8) PW7 examined the injuries of injured
Yogesh Bhatt (not examined). He also examined the
injuries of injured Sanjeev Bhatt (PW1), Rajat Singh
Bisht (not examined), Sanju Bhatt (not examined), Km.
Kanchan Bisht (not examined), Chandra Sekhar Bhatt
(PW5) and Vivek Gaur (PW2). PW8 was signatory to

5
the inquest report (Ext. Ka-10) of deceased Kedar
Singh. PW9 examined the injuries of injured Pramod
Kumar Yadav (not examined) and injured Vipin Gupta
(PW3). PW10 examined the injuries of injured Renu
Bisht and Kanak Bisht (both not examined). He also
examined the injuries of injured driver Hem Chandra
Joshi. PW11 was the Investigating Officer, who took
the statements of the witnesses, prepared site plan (Ext.
Ka-16) and submitted charge-sheet (Ext. Ka-17) against
the accused. In the cross-examination, PW11 admitted
that the accident took place all of a sudden. PW12
conducted postmortem on the dead body of Kedar
Singh and proved postmortem report (Ext. Ka-18).
PW13 inspected the jeep involved in the accident and
proved his report (Ext. Ka-19). PW13 said in the cross-examination that steering system and suspension of the
vehicle were found defective and damaged.
9) A combined reading of the testimony
rendered by the aforesaid witnesses indicated, in no
uncertain terms, that the accused was guilty of the
offences complained of against him. He was driving
the vehicle rashly and negligently. There was enough
space on the road to accommodate at least two vehicles
at a time. The road was not narrow. The plea of the
accused-revisionist that the accident took place in order
to save an incoming vehicle is contrary to the evidence
on record and is not acceptable. Prosecution evidence
was correctly appreciated by the trial court as also by

6
the lower appellate court. There is no illegality in the
judgments of two courts below. There is concurrent
findings of the trial court and the lower appellate court.
No interference is called for in the concurrent findings
of the courts below. The conviction of the accused-revisionist for the offences punishable under Sections
279, 337, 338 and 304-A of IPC is, accordingly,
affirmed.
10) Accused-revisionist was directed to undergo
six months' rigorous imprisonment alongwith a fine of
Rs. 1,000/- under Section 279 of IPC; six months'
rigorous imprisonment alongwith a fine of Rs. 500/-
under Section 337 of IPC; two years' rigorous
imprisonment alongwith a fine of Rs. 1,000/- under
Section 338 of IPC and two years' rigorous
imprisonment alongwith a fine of Rs. 2,000/- under
Section 304-A of IPC. Learned counsel for the
accused-revisionist submitted that maximum sentence
was awarded to the revisionist by the trial court for each
count, which calls for interference by this Court.
11) In State of Karnataka vs Sharanappa
Basnagouda Aregoudar; AIR 2002 S.C. 1529, Hon'ble
Apex Court in paragraph no. 7 of the judgment
observed as under:
"We are of the view that having regard to the
serious nature of the accident, which resulted in the
death of four persons, the learned single Judge should

7
not have interfered with the sentence imposed by the
Court below. It may create and set an unhealthy
precedent and send wrong signals to the subordinate
Courts which have to deal with several such accident
cases. If the accused are found guilty of rash and
negligent driving, Court have to be on guard to
ensure that they do not escape the clutches of law
very lightly. The sentence imposed by the Courts
should have deterrent effect on potential wrong-doers
and it should commensurate with the seriousness of
the offence. Of course, the Courts are given
discretion in the matter of sentence to take stock of
the wide and varying range of facts that might be
relevant for fixing the quantum of sentence, but the
discretion shall be exercised with due regard to larger
interest of the society and it is needless to add that
passing of sentence on the offender is probably the
most public face of the criminal justice system."

12) While the sentence awarded to the accused-revisionist under Sections 279 IPC and 337 IPC and
amount of fine imposed under Sections 338 IPC and
304-A IPC is not interfered with, the sentence awarded
to the accused-revisionist for the offences punishable
under Sections 338 and 304-A of IPC is modified and
the accused-revisionist is directed to undergo rigorous
imprisonment for six months under Section 338 of IPC
(alongwith fine which was imposed by the trial court)
and six months' rigorous imprisonment under Section
304-A of IPC (alongwith fine which was imposed by

8
the trial court). All the sentences shall run
concurrently. The sentence which is awarded to the
accused-revisionist in default of payment of fine shall
remain the same.
13) The accused-revisionist is on bail. His bail
is cancelled. He is directed to surrender forthwith
before the court below to serve out the sentence as
modified by this Court.
14) Let a copy of this judgment alongwith lower
court records be sent to the court below for causing the
accused-revisionist to surrender and for sending him to
prison to serve out the sentence as modified by this
Court.
15) With the modification in the sentence as
above, the criminal revision is finally disposed of.
